remove_committed_env.title: Remove the committed .env and rotate its keys
remove_committed_env.why: A secret remains exposed after it is removed from the latest revision if it is still present in Git history.
steps: Revoke and rotate every credential exposed in the file immediately
Remove the file from the repository and keep .env in .gitignore
If history must be rewritten, coordinate with collaborators and use an approved history-cleaning process; rotation is still required
Add a .env.example containing placeholder values only

write_readme.title: Write a README
write_readme.why: Recruiters often decide from the README alone.
steps: State the problem and who it is for in two sentences
Add run instructions and a screenshot
List the tech stack

improve_readme.title: Improve the existing README
improve_readme.why: A minimal existing README should explain how the project works before readers can assess it.
steps: Explain the problem, approach and important design decisions
Add architecture notes and limitations
Keep setup and usage instructions accurate

readme_metrics.title: Add meaningful measured results to the README
readme_metrics.why: Relevant, reproducible measurements help readers assess a project; invented or unsupported performance claims damage trust.
steps: Choose metrics relevant to the project and document how they are measured
Run the measurement and report results honestly, including limitations or weak results
Do not estimate or invent performance, user, or accuracy claims

add_tests.title: Add automated tests
add_tests.why: Shows you can ship code others can change safely.
steps: Add pytest (or your language's runner)
Test the core logic and one API route
Run tests with one command and document it

add_ci.title: Add CI with GitHub Actions
add_ci.why: A green badge shows the project builds and the tests pass.
steps: Add .github/workflows/ci.yml
Run install + tests on every push

add_dockerfile.title: Containerize with Docker
add_dockerfile.why: Reviewers can run your project in one command.
steps: Write a Dockerfile
Document docker build / docker run in the README

deploy_live.title: Deploy a live demo
deploy_live.why: A working live demo makes a project easier to evaluate when no existing demo or deployment configuration is detected.
steps: Confirm the project does not already have a working live demo before starting
Deploy to Render, Vercel or a similar service
Verify the deployed URL and document it in the repository

add_license.title: Add a license
add_license.why: Without one, nobody can legally reuse your code.
steps: Add an MIT or Apache-2.0 LICENSE file

add_env_example.title: Add or complete a .env.example
add_env_example.why: When the project uses environment variables, a complete placeholder example makes setup reproducible without exposing secrets.
steps: List the environment variables the project actually reads
Use safe placeholder values and never copy real credentials
Keep .env ignored by Git

add_api_layer.title: Expose the core logic as an API
add_api_layer.why: An API can demonstrate service design when it is relevant to the target role and the repository has no evidence of an existing API.
steps: Confirm the core logic is not already exposed through a working API
Wrap the relevant function in a suitable API route
Add input validation, error handling and a focused test

add_database_layer.title: Persist data in a database
add_database_layer.why: A database is a role- and project-dependent improvement, not a universal requirement.
steps: Add a database only when persistence is relevant to the project or target role
Choose an appropriate database and define a small schema
Implement and test representative queries

add_llm_feature.title: Integrate an LLM into the project
add_llm_feature.why: Consider this only when LLM integration is relevant to the target role and the project's goals.
steps: Choose a project task where an LLM is appropriate
Call a configured model through an OpenAI-compatible API
Validate outputs and document failure behavior

add_rag.title: Add retrieval (RAG) over your own data
add_rag.why: Consider retrieval only when grounding answers in a project-specific corpus supports the target role and project goals.
steps: Confirm the project needs retrieval over its own data
Chunk and embed documents and store vectors
Cite retrieved sources and evaluate retrieval quality

add_agent_loop.title: Add a tool-calling agent loop
add_agent_loop.why: Consider agents only when a tool-using workflow is relevant to the target role and project goals.
steps: Identify a task that benefits from controlled tool use
Define a small set of bounded tools and validate calls
Log and test each step, including failures

add_evals.title: Add an evaluation set and report results
add_evals.why: Evaluation separates a demo from an engineered system.
steps: Hand-label 20-50 examples
Score the system and a baseline
Report the numbers, including failures

add_statistical_analysis.title: Add a statistical analysis or experiment
add_statistical_analysis.why: Sound statistical analysis helps distinguish real effects from noise.
steps: Define a measurable question and an appropriate baseline
Choose a suitable statistical test and check its assumptions
Report effect sizes, uncertainty and limitations

deploy_model.title: Deploy or serve an ML model
deploy_model.why: A reproducible inference path shows how a model can be used beyond a notebook.
steps: Package a model behind a documented inference interface
Add input validation and a basic health check
Document how to run or deploy the service

add_ml_component.title: Add a trained or evaluated ML component
add_ml_component.why: Consider this only when applied ML is relevant to the target role and project goals.
steps: Choose a project-relevant task, model and baseline
Train and evaluate with a suitable data split
Document reproducible results and limitations

add_frontend.title: Add a simple frontend
add_frontend.why: A usable interface makes the work demonstrable.
steps: Build one page that calls your API
Handle loading and error states

add_observability.title: Add logging and basic tracing
add_observability.why: Production-minded roles ask how you debug in the field.
steps: Add structured logging
Log latency and errors per request

add_integration.title: Integrate one third-party API
add_integration.why: A focused third-party API integration can demonstrate practical systems work; partner recommendations are provided separately.
steps: Pick Slack, Jira, Google Sheets or similar
Handle auth and failures
